questions.stem: Root hair cells absorb mineral ions from the soil even when the concentration of minerals is higher inside the cell than in the soil. Which process is responsible?

options.text: Diffusion, because particles always move from high to low concentration
Osmosis, because water carries the minerals in
Active transport, because minerals are moved against the concentration gradient using energy
Evaporation from the leaves pulling minerals upward

questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances from a lower concentration to a higher concentration (against the concentration gradient). This requires energy from respiration (ATP). Root hair cells use active transport to absorb mineral ions because the concentration of minerals is usually higher inside the root than in the dilute soil solution.

questions.stem: A scientist adds a chemical that blocks ATP production to a group of cells. Which transport process would be directly affected?

options.text: Diffusion of oxygen
Osmosis of water
Active transport of glucose in the gut
Diffusion of carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Active transport requires energy from ATP, which is produced by respiration. Blocking ATP production would stop active transport but would not directly affect diffusion or osmosis, as these are passive processes that do not require energy input from the cell.

questions.stem: In the small intestine, glucose is absorbed by active transport even after its concentration is higher in the blood than in the gut. Why is this important?

options.text: It prevents glucose from being digested further
It ensures all available glucose is absorbed, maximising nutritional benefit from food
It moves glucose back into the gut for re-digestion
It converts glucose into starch for storage

questions.explanation: After a meal, diffusion initially moves glucose from the gut (high concentration) into the blood (low concentration). But as concentrations equalise, diffusion slows. Active transport continues to absorb glucose against the gradient, ensuring that as much glucose as possible is taken up from digested food rather than being lost.

questions.stem: Plants growing in waterlogged soil often show poor mineral uptake even though minerals are present. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Waterlogged soil has too many minerals, overwhelming the roots
The roots cannot carry out aerobic respiration due to lack of oxygen, reducing energy for active transport
Water dilutes the minerals so much they cannot be detected
The cell walls of root cells break down in waterlogged soil

questions.explanation: Active transport of mineral ions requires ATP from aerobic respiration. Waterlogged soil has very little oxygen available for the root cells. Without sufficient oxygen, aerobic respiration is greatly reduced, producing far less ATP, and the roots cannot actively transport minerals against the concentration gradient.

questions.stem: A student says: 'Diffusion, osmosis, and active transport are all the same because they all move substances across membranes.' What is wrong with this statement?

options.text: Only active transport moves substances across membranes
Diffusion and osmosis are passive (no energy needed) and move down the concentration gradient, while active transport requires energy and moves against it
Osmosis does not involve membranes
All three processes require ATP

questions.explanation: The key differences are: diffusion is the net movement of particles from high to low concentration (passive); osmosis is specifically the movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution (passive); active transport moves substances from low to high concentration and requires energy (ATP) from respiration.
